description: Turn OCR off entirely behind one switch ERIS_SCREEN_OCR_ENABLED (default off): no RapidOCR/Tesseract import, no backend warm-up, no pip self-heal, no background OCR, chat never forces OCR; UIA text and the cheap change detector stay. When OCR is off, explicit screen references go to the vision path on the same turn; pure anaphora keeps today's next-turn vision queue. Independent of FEAT-002 (either order after FEAT-001).
steps: Read plan.md (sections 1 D9-D11, 2 item 3, 3 checks 5-6) and context.json first.
Create src/screen/ocr_config.py with screen_ocr_enabled() (env ERIS_SCREEN_OCR_ENABLED, default '0', truthy {1,true,yes,on}, read at call time).

src/screen/ocr_worker.py: add ocr_enabled property to IncrementalScreenTextWorker; start() skips _ensure_ocr_backend when off and logs one line; _ensure_ocr_backend / _choose_ocr_backend / _auto_install_rapidocr return early when off; _capture_snapshot forces should_ocr False when off (still captures UIA/window/change ratio, never calls _prepare or backend.read); refresh_now passes force_ocr and self.ocr_enabled. Snapshot backend stays 'uia_only' via the existing branch.

src/runtime/chat_perception.py: refresh_screen_text calls refresh(force_ocr=screen_ocr_enabled()); update docstring. Confirm with a read that prepare_turn already captures immediately when mode=='vision' and needs_visual.

src/screen/screen_relevance_router.py: in the requires_strong branch and the final fallback, set needs_visual = (not screen_ocr_enabled()) and (not resolution.inherited or is_direct_vision); leave all text_evidence* branches untouched.

src/actions/capability_runtime.py runtime_sensor_health_snapshot: report 'ocr': 'disabled' when the switch is off. First grep consumers of runtime_sensor_health_snapshot and sensors['ocr'] (src/runtime/world_state.py ~l.620 and any prompt/projection code) and confirm 'disabled' is handled like browser_bridge's 'disabled'.

.env.example: add ERIS_SCREEN_OCR_ENABLED=0 with a short comment. Leave requirements*.txt alone (rapidocr-onnxruntime/onnxruntime are in no requirements file; onnxruntime is referenced only by the RapidOCR import in src/ so it is OCR-only; mention in findings).

Update existing tests that depend on OCR being on by default by adding monkeypatch.setenv('ERIS_SCREEN_OCR_ENABLED','1'): test_chat_screen_route_forces_ocr_refresh_before_vision in src/tests/test_architecture_c_runtime_regressions.py and any other test that fails only because of the new default (check test_deep_environment_native_v2.py worker tests and test_chat_evidence_ladder_v38.py). Do not change assertions.

Create src/tests/test_screen_ocr_switch.py: switch default off; worker.start()+refresh_now(force_ocr=True) with fake window/UIA/capture imports nothing (meta_path recorder for rapidocr_onnxruntime/onnxruntime/pytesseract), runs no subprocess pip, backend stays None, snapshot.backend=='uia_only'; with the switch on and a fake backend, OCR blocks are produced; ChatPerceptionCoordinator.refresh_screen_text passes force_ocr=False when off and True when on; router: explicit 'nhin man hinh di' with empty store returns mode 'vision' and needs_visual True when off, needs_visual False when on; inherited anaphora with empty store keeps needs_visual False when off and prepare_turn queues pending_vision; prepare_turn with capture_fn captures on the same turn for the explicit case and build_screen_grounding_items yields vision-derived items; capability snapshot reports ocr 'disabled' when off.

Decision point (report only): with OCR off, run the 3 real 03/11 sentences through ChatPerceptionCoordinator.prepare_turn after Eris turns that contain 'Anh'/'code' and record whether a vision capture happens now or is queued for the next turn. Put the evidence and the one-line fix suggestion (stop matching accent-folded 'anh'/'code' anchors and 'no'/'do'/'day' deictics in src/screen/screen_anaphora_rescue.py; match the accented original for 'ảnh') in findings. Do not edit screen_anaphora_rescue.py or intention_authority.py unless it is a genuine tiny change with a regression test.
acceptance_criteria: With ERIS_SCREEN_OCR_ENABLED unset, constructing and starting IncrementalScreenTextWorker never imports rapidocr_onnxruntime/onnxruntime/pytesseract, never runs pip, and never calls an OCR backend; refresh_now(force_ocr=True) does not OCR.
Chat perception never passes force_ocr=True to the worker when the switch is off.
An explicit screen reference ('nhin man hinh di') with no UIA evidence triggers vision capture on the same turn; grounding items come from the vision path.
Setting ERIS_SCREEN_OCR_ENABLED=1 restores the previous behaviour (force_ocr=True, OCR backend selection).
No crash or degraded-to-error behaviour in screen_relevance_router, evidence assembler, grounding or prompts when OCR text evidence is absent (covered by the new tests and the existing ladder tests).
Only the 3 known pre-existing failures remain in test_architecture_c_runtime_regressions.py / test_deep_environment_native_v2.py.
findings contains the false-positive evidence table and the one-line suggestion.

FOR LATER STEPS: (1) src/tests/test_run_20260811_repairs.py::test_forced_ocr_refresh_does_not_wait_forever_on_busy_capture_lock is a PRE-EXISTING problem unrelated to this FEAT: HEAD's test expects ERIS_SCREEN_CHAT_REFRESH_LOCK_TIMEOUT_SEC support in IncrementalScreenTextWorker.refresh_now, but no src code reads that variable (git grep HEAD finds it only in the test), so refresh_now blocks forever on the non-reentrant _capture_lock and the pytest process hangs. Do NOT include that file in a sweep (I killed my own hung pytest process). Not fixed: out of scope. (2) When the switch is on, behaviour is the old one (verified by tests and check 5 'switch_on_restores_old_path'). (3) With OCR off and fresh UIA text with confidence >= 0.72, route stays text_evidence (no vision), by design. (4) Docs for step 4: ocr 'disabled' in sensor_health is new; the Root/world-state prompt line 'Capability wording must match sensor_health ... UIA/OCR evidence' is unchanged (P3 out of scope).

FALSE-POSITIVE EVIDENCE (decision point, report only, no code change; measured with verify script check 6 through ChatPerceptionCoordinator.prepare_turn + real ScreenRelevanceRouter, empty evidence store). All three 03/11 sentences are classified references_screen=true, inherited=true (pure anaphora), mode=vision, route_reason=anaphora_without_screen_text_escalate_vision. Result: needs_visual=false, no capture this turn, pending_vision queued, so the NEXT turn pays one screenshot + vision call (+ the pending TTL of 30 s). It is identical with OCR on (force_ocr=true passed, same route, same pending), so the OCR switch neither creates nor worsens this cost; it only means a wrong 'screen' classification now costs a vision call instead of an OCR pass.

One-line fix suggestion: in src/screen/screen_anaphora_rescue.py stop matching accent-folded 'anh' (really 'ảnh'/'ánh'/'anh') and 'code' as PRIOR_SCREEN_ANCHORS and the bare folded deictics 'no'/'do'/'day' (really 'nó'/'đó'/'đây'); match the accented original text (e.g. 'ảnh') or require the anchor and the deictic to appear together with an imperative (xem/nhìn/đọc). Also intention_authority.py 'mo' (mở) folded matches. NOT fixed on purpose: it changes routing for real follow-ups ('nó đang chạy mà'), so it needs a product decision plus a regression suite, not a tiny safe change.
